## Edit Section Nav

The sticky anchor rail for long grouped edit forms. Each section renders as a numbered stop (01, 02…) on a vertical hairline rail; the active stop's number inverts into a filled ink chip with a subtle scale-up, and its label sharpens to the ink colour. Clicking a stop tells the consumer which section was chosen — the component itself never scrolls anything.

```gts
import { EditSectionNav } from '@cardstack/catalog/components/edit-section-nav';

<EditSectionNav
  @sections={{this.sections}}
  @activeId={{this.activeId}}
  @onSelect={{this.scrollToSection}}
/>
```

### Contract (render-only)

- `@sections: { id, label }[]` — the stops, in form order.
- `@activeId` — which stop is lit. The consumer owns this state and updates it in `@onSelect`.
- `@onSelect(id, event)` — the consumer scrolls its own section into view (scoped through the event's `closest()` root so several open edit panels never cross-scroll each other) and should mirror the active state on the target section itself (an outline ring in the same ink) so the rail and the form agree on where the reader is.
- `...attributes` ride onto the `<nav>` root, so the consumer's scoped CSS can restyle it — the usual moves are `position: sticky; top: 0` in a two-column edit grid, and flipping `flex-direction: row` (or adding the built-in `.horizontal` class) below a narrow container breakpoint.

### Colour

A reusable component asserts no brand of its own, so the rail exposes two knobs — `--edit-section-nav-ink` and `--edit-section-nav-ink-fg` — for the consuming card to point at its brand pair. Unassigned, they fall back to the theme's own `--foreground` / `--background` pair inverted, a guaranteed-contrast pairing, and never to `--primary`, which the host's edit format maps to a highlight colour that is wrong for a wayfinding rail. The active chip's halo is a `color-mix(in oklch, …)` dilution of the ink itself.

### Accessibility

Keyboard focus gets a real `:focus-visible` outline, the active stop carries `aria-current`, and `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the chip's scale and transition.

### Example

`EditSectionNavExample/contract-sections`: five contract sections beside the rail in a sticky left column; choosing a stop lights it, outlines the section and scrolls it into view.

### Consumers

The legal cards' edit forms — Contract, Addendum, Amendment, Clause, Legal Entity, Signatory — consume it unchanged; each card's ink arrives through the two knobs, never by overriding its internals.

### Non-goals

No scrolling, no scroll-spy, no hash navigation (stack rendering breaks `#anchor` hrefs), no collapsing of sections — grouping and scroll behaviour stay with the edit template that owns the form.
